title: Updating the Residency Research Requirements Presentation
goal: Locate last year's research-requirements deck, request Claude's gap and tone analysis, build the new deck skeleton, remove sensitive content and gather additional sources, draft Research Requirement and PGY timeline slides, request and review feedback on slides 1–7, share revised slide 3 for tone follow-up, build annotated Information Hub screenshot slide, gather SharePoint toolkit links for Important Links slide, draft remaining logistics slides from personal knowledge, and conduct final feedback review, date verification, and wrap-up.

Step 1.step_name: Updating the residency research requirements presentation
Step 1.step_action: Find the prior year's research-requirements deck on the laptop/OneDrive and duplicate it as the starting point for this year's version.

nodes.label: Locate last year's research requirements presentation
nodes.detail: The user recalls she is presenting on research requirements this week and needs last year's deck as a starting point. She searches her files/OneDrive to find it.

nodes.label: Open and duplicate the deck as a working template
nodes.detail: After finding the old file, she opens it in PowerPoint and makes a working copy, intending to use it as a template and hand it to Claude for review.

nodes.label: Request an update and tone-revision plan from Claude
nodes.detail: The user uploads last year's pptx and asks Claude to note what needs updating for current information and to make it sound less aggressive, citing dislike of the prior presenter's tone.

nodes.label: Analyze the deck for security, staleness, and tone issues
nodes.detail: Claude extracts the deck's text and produces a categorized report: a leaked password/email to remove immediately, stale dates/links needing current info, and scolding ALL-CAPS phrasing with softer rewrite suggestions.

nodes.label: Edit the slides
Review findings and check the slides
nodes.detail: She reads through the flagged password issue and tone examples.

nodes.label: Request step-by-step assistance to update the PowerPoint independently
nodes.detail: The participant tells Claude she wants to work through the changes piecemeal in PowerPoint herself rather than have Claude produce a full revised deck.

nodes.label: Reformat findings into a slide-by-slide punch list
nodes.detail: Claude restructures its earlier feedback into an actionable, slide-numbered checklist split into quick mechanical fixes, content needing new info, and tone rewrites, suited for manual editing.

nodes.label: Update the title slide and explore design suggestions
nodes.detail: She retitles the deck 'Research Introduction 2026-2027', decides not to include her own name, and opens PowerPoint's Designer pane looking for a cleaner title layout.

user_response.label: reject
user_response.reasoning: a3 asks what needs updating, and a8 gives the slide-by-slide punch list. She had already retitled the deck at a5 on her own, and while reading a8 she says she doesn't want her name in it. The label is reject because she doesn't use Claude's title suggestion.

nodes.label: Ask Claude how to remove the recurring footer date
nodes.detail: Stuck on how to clear the hardcoded '7/18/2025' date appearing on every slide, she asks Claude for the correct PowerPoint method.

nodes.label: Explain Header & Footer vs. Slide Master fix options
nodes.detail: Claude provides a step-by-step card recommending the Header & Footer dialog first, with the Slide Master as a fallback, since the date is likely a placeholder or layout-level text box.

nodes.label: Check the slides's title and introduction
Review the response and apply the Header & Footer fix across all slides
nodes.detail: She opens the deck in the PowerPoint desktop app, unchecks the date and slide-number options in Header & Footer, and applies the change to every slide successfully.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: a10 is the source because she asks Claude how to remove the '7/18/2025' footer date from every slide. a11 is the target because it gives the Header & Footer steps (Slide Master as fallback). She opens the deck in desktop PowerPoint, unchecks date and slide number, and clicks Apply to All, so the label is adopt: she follows Claude's steps without changes.

nodes.label: Customize the deck's color theme and background
nodes.detail: Through several rounds of trial and error in Design > Colors > Customize Colors, she settles on a gray background with an orange accent color applied consistently across the deck.

nodes.label: Review the flagged security information
nodes.detail: Rereads Claude's security warning about the personal Gmail address and plaintext password in the slide 23 notes, but leaves the notes unchanged.

user_response.label: reject
user_response.reasoning: a8 tells her to delete the personal email and password from the slide 23 notes. She reads it and says it doesn't need to be there, but she never opens the notes or removes it. The label is reject because she takes no action on the flagged security item.

nodes.label: Search email for a peer program's scholarly-activity deck
nodes.detail: Wondering whether a research requirement existed last year, she searches her Outlook inbox and downloads to locate 'Introduction to Research and Scholarly Activity at Cleveland Clinic Akron General', a related deck from another source.

nodes.label: Upload the located deck and ask Claude to extract relevant requirements
nodes.detail: She sends the newly found pptx to Claude, asking it to pull the important research-requirements info from its final section and help incorporate it into her deck.

nodes.label: Compare decks and summarize new, changed, and missing content
nodes.detail: Claude identifies content that already matches, one new bullet to add, a PGY-4 exemption discrepancy to verify with a colleague, and two entirely new policy sections (manuscript non-publication, exceptions process) to fold in.

nodes.label: Check and email, research meeting & deadlines update document and edit the slides
Review the response about comparing decks and summarize new, changed, and missing content
Locate and download a supplementary meetings/deadlines document
nodes.detail: She searches email again and downloads 'Research Meetings & Deadlines Update for CCAG.docx' to also provide to Claude as source material for the timeline slides.

nodes.label: Ask Claude to convert the deadlines document into slide-ready content
nodes.detail: She sends the downloaded meetings/deadlines docx and asks Claude to reorganize it into a format she can paste directly into the presentation.

nodes.label: Restructure the source document into PGY-year timeline content
nodes.detail: Claude reorganizes the meeting/deadline timeline into slide-ready bullets broken out by PGY-1, PGY-2, PGY-3, and ongoing expectations, flagging two ambiguous items (a likely typo, an unclear placeholder note) for her to verify.

nodes.label: Build the CCAG Research Requirement slide based on the CCAG document
nodes.detail: She captures and crops a screenshot of the attestation-style requirement text from the peer deck, pastes it into a new slide, and resizes/centers it for legibility.

nodes.label: Duplicate and populate the next PGY timeline slide
nodes.detail: She duplicates a timeline slide template and pastes in Claude's generated content for the current PGY year, removing extraneous notes she judges unnecessary ('that's dumb,' 'silly').

nodes.label: Review the research meeting & deadlines document
Review the PGY-year timeline content in the source document
Apply personal clinical knowledge to refine timeline dates
nodes.detail: Drawing on her own residency experience, she adjusts specific submission windows (IRB timing, the March 1 manuscript deadline, biostatistician turnaround) rather than relying solely on the source document.

user_response.label: modify
user_response.reasoning: a22 is the source because she asks Claude to turn the meetings/deadlines doc into slide-ready content. a23 is the target because it returns the PGY-1/2/3 timeline bullets. She pastes them into duplicated slides, drops parts she finds unnecessary, and changes dates from her own experience (earlier IRB submission, March 1 manuscript deadline, biostatistician turnaround). The label is modify because she uses Claude's structure but changes the content.

nodes.label: Rough out supporting slide headings for later sections
nodes.detail: As the timeline section solidifies, she creates placeholder headings such as 'Important Links' and reorganizes navigation-related slides in preparation for later content.

nodes.label: Request Claude's feedback on slides 1-7
nodes.detail: She uploads the in-progress deck and asks Claude for feedback and anything it would change on slides 1-7 based on the parameters discussed earlier in the session.

nodes.label: Render thumbnails and closely inspect slides 1-7 for issues
nodes.detail: Claude generates thumbnail grids and high-resolution close-ups, diagnoses a title-text-invisible-on-background bug via the slide XML, and flags leftover ALL-CAPS tone language, an ambiguous 'vs' line, and a stray placeholder question mark.

nodes.label: Capture the Akron General SharePoint navigation header, edit slides and check the CCAG document
Cross check the feedback and the slides
Confirm slide 1 is satisfactory and report that slide 2 is locked for editing
nodes.detail: The participant tells Claude slide 1 renders fine on her end (keeping it as-is) and that slide 2 is a locked document she cannot edit.

user_response.label: reject
user_response.reasoning: a31 flags the invisible title text on slide 1 and the screenshot on slide 2, among other items. She says her title renders fine and slide 2 is a locked document, and she doesn't use the rest of the feedback.

nodes.label: Acknowledge her constraints and defer on the declined items
nodes.detail: Claude explains the slide 1 rendering discrepancy is likely a viewer-specific quirk, offers an optional cosmetic tweak for slide 2's frame, and offers to continue reviewing the remaining slides.

nodes.label: Ask Claude to review the updated slide 3 and screenshot the slide
Skim Claude's acknowledgment
Report the missing attachment and request re-upload of slide 3
Share a screenshot of the revised slide 3 with Claude
nodes.detail: She takes and uploads a screenshot of the updated slide, asking for feedback on the new version.

nodes.label: Confirm the tone improvement and flag possibly dropped content
nodes.detail: Claude praises the softer language, but flags that the PGY-4 exemption line and detailed manuscript-type guidance appear to have been dropped, asking her to confirm whether that was intentional.

nodes.label: Edit the time line slides
Review the response about the revised slide and potentially missing content and check the previous screen shoot
Capture a screenshot of the SharePoint navigation for a walkthrough slide
nodes.detail: She takes a screenshot of the Akron General SharePoint homepage to use in an 'Information Hub' slide showing residents how to navigate to the research section.

user_response.label: reject
user_response.reasoning: a35a is the source because she shares the revised slide 3 and asks for feedback. a39 is the target because it praises the softer tone but flags the dropped PGY-4 exemption and the simplified manuscript-type guidance. After reading it she says 'I like all the things that I have' and leaves the slide as is, so the label is reject.

nodes.label: Insert and style a 'do not click' annotation shape
nodes.detail: She inserts a circle shape over the screenshot, sets its fill to none and outline to a thick red line, marking a navigation item residents should avoid.

nodes.label: Iteratively adjust the annotation until it clearly reads
nodes.detail: She retries the shape's fill/outline settings and repositions it multiple times so the red 'no' mark clearly overlays the correct label without hiding it.

nodes.label: Navigate SharePoint's Discover/Sites hub to find the research site
nodes.detail: She browses Discover > Sites in SharePoint and opens the 'Research & Health Sciences' site from her recent items.

nodes.label: Review the Research & Health Sciences Toolbox for relevant links
nodes.detail: She scans the toolbox page's categorized links (Research, Scholarly Activity, Scientific Session, Authorship, Manuscripts, Visiting Researchers) to decide which belong on an Important Links slide.

nodes.label: Compile selected links into the Important Links slide
nodes.detail: She builds a bullet list covering Research SharePoint items and Research Toolbox items (IRB webkit, consent form location, templates, REDCap info, statistical support requests), noting turnaround times where relevant.

nodes.label: Search for and cross-check the Application to Present Scholarly Work form
nodes.detail: She searches SharePoint for the application form, finding both a blank template and a colleague's previously completed example, reviewing the example as a reference before noting the form still needs to be properly hosted.

nodes.label: Draft the Surgical Videos slide from personal knowledge
nodes.detail: She writes out the residency's process for filming surgical video for research/teaching purposes (patient consent language, GoPro checkout logistics, camera setup, HIPAA-compliant upload workflow) entirely from her own experience.

nodes.label: Draft the Medical Student Involvement slide
nodes.detail: She lists onboarding checklist items for involving a medical student (emailing Rachida and Kalisha Washington, badge/access requirements, timeline, annual Epic/OneDrive access renewal) based on her own institutional knowledge.

nodes.label: Draft the Attending a Conference slide
nodes.detail: She writes original bullet content on conference logistics: submitting the Application to Present Scholarly Work form two weeks prior, notifying chiefs of absence, and the 10-day reimbursement submission deadline.

nodes.label: Begin building the Important People contacts slide
nodes.detail: She lists key research staff by name and role (Research Chief, Program Director, Research Managers, Biostatistician, medical-student contact), initially without email addresses.

nodes.label: Request final-draft feedback from Claude, excluding slides 1-7
nodes.detail: She uploads the near-complete deck asking Claude for any big remaining updates, explicitly noting she chose not to incorporate the earlier feedback on slides 1-7.

user_response.label: reject
user_response.reasoning: In her prompt she states she didn't incorporate any of the slides 1-7 feedback from a31, which is an explicit, document-wide rejection.

nodes.label: Inspect the final draft and flag remaining substantive issues
nodes.detail: Claude renders and reviews the deck, flagging a leftover internal note-to-self on slide 12, an inconsistent non-functional link between slides 12-13, a distracting personal-bookmarks screenshot on slide 8, a changed SMFM conference date worth verifying, an unresolved date placeholder, and a contacts slide missing emails.

nodes.label: Cross-check the flagged conference date against the official schedule
nodes.detail: Unsure whether the Scientific Session date is May 26 or June 2, she opens the department's '2026-2027 Residency Didactic Schedule' spreadsheet to verify, but finds the listed date still doesn't resolve the discrepancy.

nodes.label: Draft a confirmation email to research faculty about the date
nodes.detail: She composes an Outlook email to Bouhenni, Ruppert, and Heiselman asking them to confirm the correct Scientific Session date before she finalizes that slide.

nodes.label: Review final feedback and decide no further changes are needed
nodes.detail: She reads Claude's final-draft feedback and concludes 'Nope, this is all good. I'm done,' leaving those items unchanged.

user_response.label: reject
user_response.reasoning: a53 is the source because she asks Claude for any big remaining updates on the final draft, excluding slides 1-7. a54 is the target because it is Claude's review of that draft. It flags the slide 12 note-to-self, the slide 8 screenshot (personal bookmarks bar visible, red 'no' mark covering 'Research'), the slide 17 SMFM and SASGOG dates, and the missing emails on slide 18. After reading it she says 'Nope, this is all good. I'm done.' She leaves these items unchanged: the slide 8 screenshot still shows the bookmarks bar and the 'no' mark still covers 'Research', and no dates or contact info are changed. The label is reject because she explicitly dismisses the feedback and does not act on it.

nodes.label: Remove link-style orange formatting on slide 13 per Claude's feedback
nodes.detail: Following Claude's note that 'Application to Present Scholarly Work' on slide 13 is styled like a live hyperlink but isn't linked, she changes its font color from orange to the body-text gray (Gray-80%, Text 2) and checks that it matches the surrounding bullets.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning: a53 is the source because it is the request for final-draft feedback. a54 is the target because it is the only Claude response that raised the slide 13 link issue. Claude noted that 'Application to Present Scholarly Work' on slide 13 is orange like a live hyperlink but links nowhere, and suggested adding a real link or removing the link-style formatting. She chooses the second option: she selects the text and changes its font color from orange to the body-text gray (Gray-80%, Text 2), then checks that it matches the surrounding bullets. The label is adopt because she applies Claude's suggestion as given, without creating her own styling. This is the only a54 suggestion she acts on.
